Land. Lote 17 is an 822.56 m² parcel inside The Awen, the private gated community in Soy Tulum positioned closer to Tulum Beach than virtually any comparable land offering. At $550 USD per square meter, it sits below the project's $600/m² list rate, an entry point that leaves room for appreciation as the macro project moves toward official launch. The Awen is a limited release of 58 lots, with less than 10% of inventory remaining. The community sits roughly 2,500 ft from the middle of the Hotel Zone, with private access roads connecting owners and guests directly to Tulum's best-known clubs and bars, and the beach itself is 900 meters away. Access runs through two security checkpoints, making it one of the most secure projects in Tulum, an attribute that carries real weight with high-end buyers who value privacy. The Awen impacts only 30% of the project footprint, preserving trees and wildlife across the balance, and stands as one of the lowest-impact developments in the area. Amenities are built for the community rather than bolted on: a lap pool, contemplation paths, an organic garden, a wellness center running yoga, Pilates and mindfulness classes, a beach club, and beach access under a kilometer away. At 822.56 m², Lote 17 sits comfortably in the buildable middle of The Awen's range, generous enough for a substantial villa with pool and garden while staying within the community's low-density design language. Proximity to the beach with permits in place means comparable supply is limited, which supports a straightforward exit when an owner chooses to sell. Financing runs on a 35% downpayment with the remaining 65% not payable for 18 months, carrying no monthly payments or fees. Coastal zone note: properties in this area fall under Mexico's restricted zone, and foreign buyers acquire through a fideicomiso (bank trust). Our team can walk you through the structure. 📍 Location: The Awen, Soy Tulum, Quintana Roo 🌴 Position: Private gated community, 900 m from the beach, 2,500 ft from the Hotel Zone ⛲️ Amenities: Swimming pool with lanes Beach club and beach access Wellness center (yoga, Pilates, mindfulness) Organic garden and contemplation paths Club house Gym Two security checkpoints 📏 Lot Size sqm: 822.56 m² 📐 Lot Size: 8,854 sq ft 💵 Price x m²: USD $550 💵 Total Price: USD $452,408 ⏳ Payment Plan: Ask your broker for payment plans and special offers ‍

Finished property. Villa Asha is a two-storey residence in Aldea Premium, one of Tulum's most exclusive gated communities, minutes by bike or car from downtown and the Hotel Zone. Designed following Feng Shui and Vaastu principles, the villa is a sanctuary of elegant simplicity surrounded by the Mayan jungle. Floor to ceiling glass doors open onto a central courtyard with a private pool and a living wall, seamlessly connecting indoor and outdoor living. The social floor is arranged around it: a designer kitchen and dining area at one end, an open plan living space at the other, with a study, daybed, and full bathroom alongside. Wraparound glass carries the jungle into every room. Upstairs, three bedrooms open off a light-filled hall. The primary suite has a king bed, a private sitting area, two air conditioning units, ceiling fans, and an en suite bathroom. The second and third bedrooms each hold a queen bed with air conditioning and ceiling fans, sharing a large, bright bathroom, and one opens onto a balcony above the tropical canopy. Front and rear patios give the villa two distinct outdoor moods, one for morning light and one for star filled Tulum nights. Built in 2022 and delivered turnkey, Villa Asha is ready to occupy or to place into Tulum's short term rental market. Reduced from $720,000 USD to $626,000 USD. 📍 Location: Aldea Premium, Tulum, Quintana Roo 🌴 Position: Gated community, minutes from Tulum centre and the Hotel Zone ⛲️ Key Features: 4 bedrooms, 3 bathrooms across 2 levels Central courtyard with private pool and living wall Feng Shui and Vaastu design principles Floor to ceiling wraparound glass Designer kitchen with island and dining area Study with daybed and full bathroom on the social floor Primary suite with private sitting area and en suite Balcony over the tropical canopy Front and rear patios Parking Turnkey, built 2022 📏 Construction: 292 m² / 3,143 sq ft 📐 Lot: 335.10 m² / 3,607 sq ft 💵 Price: $626,000 USD (reduced from $720,000 USD) ‍ ‍

Finished property. Villa Illume | 4 Bedroom Designer Villa in Aldea Premium, Tulum Tucked near the end of a quiet cul de sac in Aldea Premium, Villa Illume sits inside one of Tulum's smallest and most guarded residential enclaves, just 36 homes in total. The neighbors are multimillion dollar estates. The price is not. The ground floor opens into a single connected volume of kitchen, dining, and living space beneath three meter ceilings finished in wooden inlay and lit from a recessed cove. A full wall of sliding glass retracts entirely, so the room ends at a lap pool that runs the length of the garden with jungle canopy rising behind it. A covered pergola lounge and a stone outdoor kitchen sit alongside, which means dinner for ten happens without anyone deciding whether they are inside or out. The second floor holds the bedrooms, each with its own bath, arranged along a corridor lit from a skylight above rather than windows onto the street. Bedrooms open to planted terraces. The top floor belongs to the principal suite alone, with a private terrace, a plunge pool set against a stone wall, a lounge under a wood pole canopy, and a half bath. The house was completed in 2022 and has been kept to a standard that matches the enclave around it: travertine floors, chukum walls, solid wood cabinetry and doors throughout, and stone basins cut for each bath. What makes it unusual is not the finish level or the design. It is that a home of this quality exists in Aldea Premium at this number. 📍 Location: Aldea Premium, Aldea Zamá, Tulum, Quintana Roo 🌴 Position: Near the end of a private cul de sac, 36 home enclave, 24/7 security ⛲️ Key Features: Open concept kitchen, dining, and living on the ground floor 3 m / 9.8 ft ceilings with wooden inlay and cove lighting Full width retracting glass wall to pool terrace Lap pool with jungle backdrop and covered pergola lounge Stone outdoor kitchen and bar Rooftop principal suite with private terrace, plunge pool, lounge, and half bath Bedrooms en suite, several with terrace access Walk in closet with safe in principal suite Chukum finishes and travertine floors throughout Solid wood cabinetry, doors, and custom stone basins Skylit interior corridor with glass balustrade Maid's quarters and guest bath on ground level Garage parking Built 2022 📐 Lot Size: 304.25 m² / 3,275 sq ft 📏 Construction: 299.5 m² / 3,224 sq ft total Ground floor: 107.2 m² / 1,154 sq ft Second floor: 99.8 m² / 1,074 sq ft Third floor: 77.7 m² / 836 sq ft Pool: 18.9 m² / 203 sq ft 🛏️ Bedrooms: 4 🛁 Bathrooms: 4.5 💵 Price: $650,000 USD ‍

Finished property. Villa Las Almas sits on a residential street in Aldea Zamá, the only fully developed neighborhood in Tulum, where the houses share a single architectural language and the street reads as a neighborhood rather than a construction site. The lot backs onto standing jungle, so the trees behind the property are the view from every rear window. The ground floor is one continuous volume. Kitchen, dining, and living run together and open through sliding glass onto a covered terrace, a gravel garden planted with palms, and a pool set at the far edge under the tree line. Travertine runs from the interior straight out to the terrace, so the floor never changes underfoot when you step outside. Upstairs the plan opens into a second lounge on the landing, which gives the house a family room that is separate from the main social floor. The bedrooms run off it, each with jungle on the other side of the glass, and the principal opens onto its own terrace behind a glass balustrade. Cabinetry, headboards, and shelving are solid tropical hardwood throughout, built in rather than bought. At 267 m² on a 360 m² lot, the house is sized for a family or a rental operator who needs real bed count without a trophy estate's carrying costs. It comes furnished as photographed. 📍 Location: Aldea Zamá, Tulum, Quintana Roo 🌴 Position: Residential street backing onto jungle, uniform neighboring architecture ⛲️ Key Features: Open plan kitchen, dining, and living on the ground floor Full width sliding glass to covered terrace and garden Pool set against the jungle tree line Second lounge on the upper landing Principal bedroom with private terrace and glass balustrade Solid hardwood cabinetry, headboards, and built in shelving Travertine floors inside and out Air conditioning and ceiling fans throughout Furnished as photographed 📐 Lot Size: 360 m² / 3,875 sq ft 📏 Construction: 267 m² / 2,874 sq ft 🛏️ Bedrooms: 5 💵 Price: $749,000 USD ‍

desc.en: Lot 22 runs from the Caribbean to the lagoon inside the Sian Ka'an Biosphere Reserve, a UNESCO World Heritage site whose Mayan name means Origin of the Sky. Over 12 acres, with 100 metres of beachfront at the front and the same again at the lagoon behind. The lot is flat and set with palm trees, one of the more buildable shapes among the Sian Ka'an lots, and carries density to build a home of approximately 4,300 sq ft. Around it sit tropical forest, mangrove and marsh, a barrier reef offshore, and habitat for more than 300 bird species. Reached at Km 31, past the arches of Sian Ka'an. desc.en: Finished property. Pure Tulum 403 is a corner penthouse in a boutique building of only fifteen residences, two blocks from Aldea Zamá's commercial core and two from the new road to the beaches. The building is the work of Tacher Architects, designed bioclimatically so breezes cross the living areas and bedrooms, with interiors by B Huber and a staggered prism form that leaves no residence overlooked. A private elevator opens from the lobby directly into the apartment, where dining, kitchen and living run open onto a 568 sq ft terrace with its own plunge pool, kitchen bar and room to dine and lounge, all on one level. The principal bedroom holds an en suite bath and windows on two sides; both bedrooms have floor to ceiling glass with vertical privacy beams, facing protected green areas. Finishes run to chukum walls, local hardwood cabinetry, ojinaga marble floors and SMEG appliances. 📍 Location: Aldea Zamá, Tulum, Quintana Roo 🌴 Position: Two blocks to Aldea Zamá commercial areas, two blocks to the beach road ⛲️ Features: Corner penthouse in a boutique building of 15 residences Private elevator access direct from the lobby 568 sq ft terrace with private plunge pool and kitchen bar Open plan dining, kitchen and living on a single level Principal bedroom with en suite bath and dual aspect windows Floor to ceiling windows overlooking protected green areas Chukum finish walls, local hardwood cabinetry, ojinaga marble floors SMEG kitchen appliances Laundry room with stackable washer and dryer Building pool in Bali stone with baja shelf and hammocks Two fitness rooms, juice bar, lobby, security guard on duty Bioclimatic design by Tacher Architects, interiors by B Huber 🛏 Bedrooms: 2 🛁 Bathrooms: 2 📏 Size: 144 m² (~1,548 sqft) 💵 Total Price: $365,000 USD ‍

Finished property. Casa Cenote is a beachfront commercial property in Tankah Bay, assembled from three adjoining lots across 3,279.30 m² with 745.38 m² of construction. In operation today as an eleven room boutique hotel with a restaurant and bar, a small grocery and a storage area, it is a working business on the sand rather than a project waiting to begin. For a buyer planning a larger development, it offers the rare position of holding a beachfront site that trades while the next phase is designed. The Hotel Eleven rooms accommodate up to thirty guests. Four rooms carry double beds sleeping up to four, and seven are configured for two, a mix that suits group bookings and extended stays as readily as nightly guests. Restaurant, Bar and Services A restaurant and bar serve both guests and passing trade, supported by a small grocery and a dedicated storage area. The infrastructure is in place and the operation is established, which shortens the path for an incoming owner considerably. The Land Three adjoining lots totalling 3,279.30 m² give the site scale unusual for beachfront Tankah, with frontage on one of the quieter bays between Tulum and Akumal. Buyers should verify permitted density, land use and any development approvals independently. Singular by the Sea Casa Cenote is shown by private appointment only, with operational detail and financials released to qualified buyers on request. Serious enquiries are warmly invited. 📍 Location: Tankah Bay, Quintana Roo 🌴 Position: Beachfront, three adjoining lots ⛲️ Features: 11 room boutique hotel accommodating up to 30 guests 4 rooms with double beds sleeping up to 4 7 rooms configured for 2 guests Restaurant and bar Small grocery store Storage area Three adjoining lots Currently operating 🏨 Rooms: 11 (sleeps up to 30) 📏 Size: 745 m² (~8,023 sqft) construction on a 3,279 m² (~35,298 sqft) lot 💵 Total Price: $6,500,000 USD ‍

Finished property. Set on the upper floor of a boutique residence at the eastern edge of Aldea Zamá, Amira Residence looks out over the treeline to the sea. Four bedrooms, four full bathrooms, and 177 square meters arranged for the way life actually moves here: long mornings on the terrace with the water in view, afternoons in the pool, evenings that drift from the dining room to the solarium without anyone deciding to go anywhere. The Residence Four bedrooms, each with its own full bathroom Living room and separate dining room Full kitchen Private terrace and garden Sea views from the upper floor Individual air conditioning throughout Delivered two years ago, in move in condition Building and Amenities Swimming pool Rooftop solarium with open sightlines Fitness center Two common lounge areas Underground parking 24 hour security The Setting Amira sits on the eastern side of Aldea Zamá, the stretch closest to the coast, where the density drops and the jungle canopy gives way to open sky. That position is what puts the sea in view from the upper floors, a rarity this far back from the beach road. Aldea Zamá itself remains the most established address in Tulum: paved streets, reliable services, restaurants and boutiques minutes away. desc.en: Finished property. Casa Liana climbs three levels through the canopy of La Veleta, ending at a rooftop pool that sits level with the treetops. Inside, double height glazing pulls the jungle into the living space, and the material palette stays deliberately quiet: polished chukum, warm timber, woven pendant lighting. It is a house built to disappear into its surroundings rather than announce itself against them. The Residence Two bedrooms Three bathrooms Three levels Double height living area with full height windows Sculptural open staircase 177 m² of construction on a 202 m² lot Rooftop Private pool at canopy level Open terrace with jungle outlook The Setting La Veleta has become the address for buyers who want Tulum without the hotel zone. The streets are quieter, the lots are larger, and the jungle still has the upper hand. Cafés, wellness studios, and restaurants have filled in steadily over the past few years, and the town center sits a short drive away. It is where the design driven side of Tulum construction has concentrated. 📍 La Veleta, Tulum 🌴 Three level residence with rooftop pool ⛲️ Private pool, jungle outlook, double height living 🛏 2 bedrooms 🛁 3 bathrooms 📏 177 m² construction / 1,905 sq ft, 202 m² lot / 2,174 sq ft 💵 USD 625,000

Land. Two thousand seven hundred seventy five square meters fronting the Bacalar lagoon, four kilometers from the municipal center and steps from downtown. This is a clean, buildable parcel with the paperwork already done: escritura in hand, soil mechanics study complete, topographic survey complete, property tax paid current, and an updated cedula catastral. The lot sits between Prolongación Costero Sur and the federal lagoon zone, with 24.98 meters of lagoon frontage and a depth running just over 111 meters. Zoning and Build Potential The parcel carries ZTA classification under the Bacalar urban development program, which permits national and international tourism use alongside private or alternative residential development. Approved project types include concept hotels, vacation rental villas, glamping, and holistic centers. Density allows 15 rooms per hectare or 8 dwellings per hectare. Maximum height is two levels or 8 meters. CUS 1.00 and COS 30 percent. Federal Zone Note Ten meters of ZOFEMAT federal maritime land sit in front of the property. This strip can be cleared, maintained, and used for decking. No ZOFEMAT concession has been granted on this parcel to date. Buyers should note that federal zone land remains public by law and access cannot be legally restricted, though in practice this is uncommon in the area. A concession application is the standard route for owners seeking formal rights over the strip. Access and Services Dirt road access at 200 meters. Electric service 100 meters from the property line. There is no municipal water in the area; a well is viable on the parcel. Direct lagoon access from the frontage. The Setting Bacalar's Laguna de los Siete Colores draws travelers for water that shifts from pale turquoise to deep indigo across the day. The town has grown steadily as a slower alternative to the Riviera Maya coast, and lagoon front land at this size and this proximity to the center is limited by simple geography. The shoreline is finite and most of what remains at scale sits well outside the urban core. 📍 Bacalar, Quintana Roo 🌴 Lagoon front, ZTA zoning ⛲️ Well viable, electric 100m, dirt road 200m 📏 2,775.99 m² / 29,880 sq ft 🛣 24.98 m lagoon frontage 💵 $11,000,000 MXN (approx. $600,000 USD) ‍ ‍

Finished property. Four hundred sixty seven square meters of finished construction on a 321 square meter lot in El Mirador, delivered turnkey and ready to occupy. Polished concrete runs throughout, offset by reclaimed wood ceilings, volcanic stone facing, and marble surfaces that catch the light from floor to ceiling glazing on every level. The entry crosses a reflecting channel of water before the house opens into a single continuous volume of kitchen, dining, and lounge that folds out to the pool. Living and Kitchen The main level runs as one open floor. A double island kitchen in marble and dark timber anchors the space, with full appliance package, breakfast seating for four at the counter, and a dining table seating twelve beneath a slatted timber ceiling and pendant array. Sliding glass panels retract to the pool deck and outdoor bar with grill, making the interior and terrace read as one room. Bedrooms and Bathrooms Six bedrooms across the upper floors, several with private terrace access and jungle outlook, others configured with twin kings for larger groups. Five and a half bathrooms finished in polished concrete with rain showers, black stone vessel basins, and reclaimed timber detailing. Primary suites open directly to planted terraces. Outdoor and Rooftops Two separate rooftops. The lower terrace holds the main pool with sun deck, shaded bar, and mature palm planting enclosed by privacy walls. The upper roof carries a plunge pool under a timber pergola with open views across the jungle canopy toward the coast. Included Membership Ownership includes Ahau Hotels vacation club membership benefits, extending access across the group's Tulum properties. 📍 El Mirador, Tulum 🌴 Two rooftops, pool and plunge pool, outdoor bar and grill ⛲️ Ahau Hotels vacation club membership included 🛏 6 bedrooms 🛁 5.5 bathrooms 📏 Land 321 m² / 3,455 sq ft 📏 Construction 467 m² / 5,027 sq ft 💵 $1,550,000 USD ‍

Finished property. Set within La Privada, one of Aldea Zamá's most established gated enclaves, Casa Abaton rises across three levels and a rooftop terrace. Six bedrooms, two swimming pools and a level of finish that reads immediately on arrival. Six bedrooms, six full bathrooms plus two half baths High end finishes and equipment throughout Ground floor swimming pool Rooftop swimming pool and terrace Three level layout with clear separation of living and sleeping areas La Privada Amenities Gated community with controlled access and 24/7 security Club house Community swimming pool Padel court Restaurants, fresh market and convenience store directly across the street Ahau Hotels Vacation Club Membership included Location Aldea Zamá remains the most complete address in Tulum. Paved streets, full services, walkable retail and a fifteen minute drive to the beach. La Privada sits inside that grid with its own layer of privacy and security. 📍 La Privada, Aldea Zamá, Tulum 🌴 3 stories plus rooftop terrace ⛲️ Two pools plus full La Privada amenity package 🛏 6 Bedrooms 🛁 6.5 Bathrooms 📏 360 m² / 3,875 sq ft construction | 380 m² lot + 130 m² 💵 $1,680,000 USD ‍

📍 Location Punta Brava, Puerto Morelos, Quintana Roo 🌴 Position Beachfront, five kilometers south of the village, at the end of the coastal road The coastal road out of Puerto Morelos runs south past the last of the houses, past the last of the pavement, and then simply stops. What waits at the end of it is 2,400 m² / 25,834 sq ft of raw Caribbean shoreline, three contiguous parcels laid side by side across sixty linear meters of open coast, with a saltwater inlet gathering at the edge of the sand like a natural pool cut into the rock. There is nothing built here. No hotel, no beach club, no vehicles, almost no one. A slender steel lighthouse stands on the point immediately beside the land, white against the water, and beyond it the reef breaks in a long line of surf. This is the beginning of the Riviera Maya corridor, the stretch that runs another 130 kilometers south toward Punta Allen without interruption. The Land Three rectangular parcels, Lots 3, 4 and 5, each measuring 40 by 20 meters for 800 m² / 8,611 sq ft apiece. The topography is regular and level throughout, requiring no terracing or fill. Each lot fronts the federal maritime zone on its eastern boundary and a projected street on its western, giving the assembled site clean access on both sides. Held together they form an unbroken 60 meter / 197 ft ribbon of coast, a frontage width that has become extremely difficult to assemble anywhere north of Tulum. What the Municipality Permits The parcels sit within Tourist Coastal zoning under the Puerto Morelos Urban Development Program published in February 2026. The assigned code is TE/3/50/M1: 30% land coverage, a floor area ratio of 1.0, three levels, and a maximum height of 10.5 meters. Setbacks run five meters front and rear with two meters on one lateral. Density is set at 25 dwellings or 50 rooms per hectare. Within the surrounding management unit the environmental policy is one of sustainable use, with soil, mangrove and biodiversity listed as priority resources. The envelope suits a private beachfront residence, a small collection of villas, or a low density boutique property. The Setting Puerto Morelos kept what its neighbors traded away. It is a working fishing village with a leaning lighthouse on the main pier, a square ringed by seafood restaurants and artisan stalls, and a pace that runs on foot and by bicycle rather than by car. The reef offshore belongs to the second largest barrier reef system in the world and lies close enough to shore to swim to. Inland, the Route of the Cenotes threads some 35 kilometers past dozens of open, closed and semi open cenotes. Cancún International sits 20 to 30 minutes north, Playa del Carmen 33 kilometers south, and a Tren Maya station now links the village to the wider peninsula. Dolphins and sea turtles are seen regularly along this stretch of water. ⛲️ Features ⛲️ Three contiguous beachfront parcels totaling 2,400 m² / 25,834 sq ft ⛲️ 60 linear meters / 197 ft of open Caribbean frontage ⛲️ Each parcel 40 by 20 meters, 800 m² / 8,611 sq ft ⛲️ Level, regular topography across the full site ⛲️ Tourist Coastal zoning, three levels, 10.5 m maximum height ⛲️ 25 dwellings or 50 rooms per hectare permitted density ⛲️ Projected street access on the western boundary ⛲️ Saltwater inlet forming a natural pool at the shoreline ⛲️ Historic Punta Brava lighthouse adjacent to the land ⛲️ Puerto Morelos Reef National Park offshore ⛲️ 20 to 30 minutes from Cancún International Airport ⛲️ Virgin beach setting with no commercial development Ownership Punta Brava lies within Mexico's restricted coastal zone. Foreign buyers acquire through a fideicomiso, a bank trust granting full rights of use, lease, improvement, inheritance and sale. Mexican nationals and Mexican corporations hold title directly. The eastern boundary of each parcel adjoins ZOFEMAT, the federal maritime terrestrial zone, and any use of that strip is governed by federal concession rather than by private title. Buyers should verify concession status, boundaries and permitting with independent counsel. Land of this width, on open coast, this close to the airport, is not being made anymore. 📏 2,400 m² / 25,834 sq ft 🌊 60 m / 197 ft frontage 💵 USD $2,358,000 ‍

desc.en: Pre-construction. 📍 Location Faena District, Tulum, Quintana Roo 🌴 Position Building A, garden or upper level, facing the amenity gardens Residence A is the smallest thing Faena builds here and the most precisely made. One bedroom, one bathroom, and a single continuous living and dining volume that opens across the full seven meter width of the plan onto a covered terrace. Interior area is 70.30 m² / 756.7 sq ft with 11.20 m² / 120.6 sq ft of covered terrace beyond it. Burnt sienna screens close across that opening when the afternoon turns and the room fills with barred gold light instead of heat. The kitchen is fully equipped and set into the wall rather than marooned on an island, which is what lets a plan this size read as generous rather than compact. The bathroom carries a soaking tub. The roof above holds shared pools and amenities for the building rather than a private terrace, and that is the trade that puts a Faena address within reach at this number. Total area 81.5 m² / 877.3 sq ft. Two remain. A garden level residence at USD $802,500 and an upper level residence at USD $832,000.

Pre-construction. 📍 Location Faena District, Tulum, Quintana Roo 🌴 Position Level 2, private rooftop with pool The B2 sits one floor up from the gardens and takes its outdoor space upward instead of outward. Interior area is 95.24 m² / 1,025.2 sq ft across two bedrooms and two and a half bathrooms, with a covered terrace of 30.80 m² / 331.5 sq ft running off the living volume. The roof above belongs to the residence alone: 45 m² / 484.4 sq ft holding a pool 6.9 meters long, an outdoor kitchen and shaded lounge space. The advantage of level two over level three is the canopy. At this height the trees are still around you rather than below, and the terrace sits inside the green rather than above it. The living, dining and kitchen volume runs uninterrupted across the plan, bedrooms behind their own circulation. Bathrooms carry double vanities, mosaic detail and a soaking tub. Finished property. 📍 Location Los Árboles Tulum, Carretera Tulum Nuevo Xcán 🌴 Position Five acre jungle lot, gated, fifteen minutes from downtown Tulum Two hectares of high canopy jungle, and a house that occupies almost none of it. Los Árboles caps construction at five percent of any lot, so what surrounds this residence is not landscaping that a neighbour might one day clear. It is jungle, and it stays jungle, part of a preserve running to twelve hundred acres. Toucans and monkeys move through it. The nearest sound is the community gate, and that is a long way off. The house runs on one level, 260 m² / 2,799 sq ft of interior opening onto 91 m² / 980 sq ft of covered terrace and a further 307 m² / 3,305 sq ft of outdoor living. Three bedrooms, three bathrooms and a half, all air conditioned. The plan is built around water: a lap pool of 21 meters, seventy feet, finished in black metallic tile so it reads as a dark line cut through the green rather than a blue rectangle dropped into it. Long enough to actually swim. The Terraces There are two, and they do different jobs. The first sits under a pergola with seating for sixteen, which is the number that turns a house into a place people gather. The second is quieter, built against a waterfall wall, with a life size jaguar carved from zapote wood standing in it. Zapote is the wood the Maya used for lintels because it outlasts everything, and the piece was made by hand. Beyond both, garden and patio give way to jungle without a fence line to interrupt them. The Systems Los Árboles is an off grid community, so this is not a house that depends on the grid arriving. Solar panels carry it, lithium batteries hold the charge overnight, and a generator sits behind both of those. Starlink handles connectivity, which matters more here than it would in town. A water softener runs throughout and the fixtures are Moen under lifetime warranty, the sort of specification that only shows itself years later. Dogs are welcome. Furnishings are negotiable. Features 🌳 Five acre lot, 20,234 m² / 217,799 sq ft, within a twelve hundred acre preserve 🏊 Lap pool of 21 m / 70 ft in black metallic tile 🏡 Single level plan, three bedrooms, three and a half bathrooms 🍽 Pergola covered terrace seating sixteen 🐆 Waterfall terrace with life size zapote jaguar ☀️ Solar array, lithium storage and backup generator 📡 Starlink connectivity 🔒 Gated community with security around the clock Ownership Tulum sits within Mexico's restricted zone. Foreign buyers acquire through a fideicomiso, a bank trust granting full rights of use, lease, improvement, inheritance and sale. Mexican nationals and Mexican corporations hold title directly. Los Árboles carries a homeowners association fee of USD $1,700 and community rules governing land use, materials and construction footprint. Buyers should review the HOA statutes and confirm areas, systems and fee terms independently. 🛏 3 🛁 3.5 📏 260 m² / 2,799 sq ft interior 🌳 20,234 m² / 5 acres lot 💵 USD $600,000

Finished property. 📍 Location Región 15, Tulum 🌴 Position One street from Avenida Kukulkán, fifteen minutes from the Hotel Zone and the beach The Approach A solid timber gate set into a white wall, banana leaf pushing against it, and then the sound of water. Bang Bao Villa keeps everything behind that line. From the street it gives away nothing. Inside, a courtyard opens around a private pool with the house wrapped on two sides, palm trunks rising past the second floor balconies, chukum walls holding the light the way only chukum does. The House Three bedrooms across two levels, three bathrooms, four beds. The ground floor runs open from the entry through to the pool, glass doors folding back so the living room becomes terrace and the terrace becomes courtyard. Built in seating along one wall, a long timber table under a beam light fixture, kitchen fully equipped and ready to cook in tonight. Upstairs the bedrooms take the canopy views, sliding doors to private balconies, palms at eye level. The material language is restrained and consistent. Polished cement floors, chukum and lime plaster, tzalam and parota joinery, woven and macramé textiles. Nothing here is provisional. The house was finished, furnished, and put straight into service. The Courtyard The pool sits at the centre of the plot rather than at the edge of it, which is the reason the house works. Sun beds and pool chairs on the deck, palms filtering the afternoon, thatch on the boundary wall. It holds twelve people for dinner or one person with coffee at seven in the morning and reads correctly either way. The Lot Beside It This is what separates Bang Bao from every other finished villa in Región 15. The empty parcel next door belongs to the same owner and comes with the house as an option, not an obligation. Take the villa on its own 242.575 m² and you have a complete, operating, income producing home. Add the lot and you control the frontage, with room for a second build, a guest structure, a larger garden, or simply the certainty that nothing goes up on the other side of your wall. The parcel is approximately 2,000 m² / 21,528 sq ft. The owner will also divide it and sell half at 1,000 m² / 10,764 sq ft. Land at this level inside Región 15, one street from Avenida Kukulkán, is not something that comes back around. The Position Región 15 sits between La Veleta and the coast, with Aldea Zamá directly across Avenida Kukulkán. The house is one street off the avenue, which puts the commercial strip, the Mistiq developments, and the Kukulkán access corridor to the beach within a few minutes. Fifteen minutes to the Hotel Zone. Región 15 has moved faster on price per square metre than almost anywhere else in Tulum, and the properties holding that value are the ones with real construction on real title rather than another studio in another tower. The Numbers The owner reports strong and consistent rental performance, and the house currently operates as a short term rental with furniture, equipment, and operating setup in place. Reported returns should be verified independently by the buyer against booking records and financials before any offer is made. Three Ways to Buy Villa only, on its 242.575 m² / 2,611 sq ft lot. $550,000 USD Villa plus half the adjacent lot, total 1,242.575 m² / 13,375 sq ft. $689,000 USD Villa plus the full adjacent lot, total 2,242.575 m² / 24,139 sq ft. $828,000 USD Ownership Tulum sits inside Mexico's restricted zone, within 50 km of the coastline. Foreign buyers acquire through a fideicomiso, a bank trust granting full rights of use, lease, sale, and inheritance, or through a Mexican corporation where the use case supports it. Standard, routine, and handled at closing. 🛏 3 Bedrooms 🛁 3 Bathrooms 📏 Lot 242.575 m² / 2,611 sq ft 💵 From $550,000 USD

Finished property. 📍 Location Región 15, Tulum 🌴 Position Manzana 189 on 25 Poniente bis, eight minutes from Tulum Beach The Idea The walls are made of coconut husk. Not clad in it, not accented with it. The structural walls of this house are built from coconut fiber, an agricultural byproduct that Quintana Roo produces in volume and usually burns or buries. Thirty centimetres thick. That single decision changes everything downstream, and it is the reason this house does not look, feel, or behave like the concrete boxes going up around it. The House Three levels, 210 m² / 2,260 sq ft of construction on a 145.7 m² / 1,568 sq ft lot. The ground floor opens as one continuous run: integral kitchen with stone countertops and custom hardwood cabinetry, breakfast area, pantry, living room, half bath, and floor to ceiling glass sliding back onto a private plunge pool and a 19 m² / 205 sq ft garden. One parking space. The second level holds both bedrooms, each with a full bathroom, custom wardrobes in woven cane and hardwood, and the acoustic quiet that thick fiber walls produce naturally. Morning light comes through sheer curtains onto the canopy. The third level is given over entirely to leisure. A rooftop garden with a built in bar and open views across the Región 15 treeline, which at this height means jungle in every direction rather than the neighbours. The Material Coconut fiber walls provide thermal and acoustic insulation that concrete cannot. Interiors stay cooler and quieter without leaning on air conditioning, which is the practical benefit a buyer feels every single day in Tulum. The developer reports that the walls absorb CO2 as they cure and continue to strengthen with age rather than degrade, and cites annual energy savings above 60 percent against conventional construction. These are the developer's figures and are not independently certified. Buyers should request the supporting documentation directly. Around it, the architecture is built to move air. High ceilings, large format windows, cross ventilation designed so heat rises and escapes rather than collecting. The house breathes. The Water In place of a conventional septic tank, the project runs a biodigester paired with a constructed wetland. Organic matter breaks down biologically, then plants and natural substrates finish the purification before water returns to the ground. In a town built on a limestone shelf riddled with cenotes and underground rivers, that is not a marketing gesture. It is the difference between a house that sits on the aquifer and a house that protects it. The Position Región 15 sits between La Veleta and the coast, with Aldea Zamá across Avenida Kukulkán. This particular pocket, Manzana 189 on 25 Poniente bis, keeps a high density of original vegetation and quiet streets, and reads as a neighbourhood built for people who actually live here rather than a corridor of short term rental inventory. The immediate surroundings include Atman Residences, Mistiq Gardens, Naia Tulum, and Jungle Villas. Eight minutes to the sand. The Scarcity There are two villas. That is the entire project. Unit 1 currently serves as the showroom and is ready for immediate delivery. Unit 2 is under construction with delivery projected for 2027. When both are placed, there is no third. The Terms List price 7,950,000 MXN per villa, approximately $461,000 USD at current rates, which works out to roughly 37,857 MXN per square metre of construction. Three payment structures are available: Cash. 90 percent on signing with a 5 percent discount, 10 percent on delivery. 30 60 10. 30 percent down, 60 percent across construction interest free, 10 percent on delivery. 50 40 10. 50 percent down, 40 percent across construction interest free, 10 percent on delivery. USD figures move with the exchange rate. Pricing is set in Mexican pesos. Ownership Tulum sits inside Mexico's restricted zone, within 50 km of the coastline. Foreign buyers acquire through a fideicomiso, a bank trust granting full rights of use, lease, sale, and inheritance, or through a Mexican corporation where the use case supports it. Standard, routine, and handled at closing. 🛏 2 Bedrooms 🛁 2.5 Bathrooms 📏 210 m² / 2,260 sq ft 💵 $461,000 USD

Sian Ka'an translates from Maya as the gate of heaven, or the place where the sky begins. The name has held for a thousand years and it still does the work of description better than any brochure line. This is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a federally protected biosphere reserve, a corridor of white sand, mangrove, palm forest and shallow reef running south from Tulum along one of the last undeveloped coastlines in the Mexican Caribbean. Land inside the reserve does not come to market. Land inside the reserve that is cleared to build almost never does. Section I This listing is Section I: 12,114.34 m² / 130,399 sq ft at USD $2,422,868, which is USD $200 per square metre. It runs the full width of the peninsula, meeting the Caribbean on its eastern boundary and the lagoon system on its western. That geometry is the entire point. Sunrise over open water on one side, sunset across still lagoon on the other, and a private crossing between them held in a single title. Access is by the coastal sand road that threads the peninsula, palm canopy closing overhead in places, the beach never more than a few steps beyond the tree line. A timber dock already sits on the lagoon edge. Permitted to Build The owner states that construction permits are in place across the holding, and that support extends past the closing table: guidance through the build itself and assistance securing any further authorizations the project requires. For a site of this kind that continuity is worth as much as the permits. The people who obtained them know the agencies, the precedents and the sequence, and that knowledge does not transfer in a document folder. Permit scope, current validity and transferability should be confirmed directly with the issuing authorities before closing. Full documentation is available for buyer and counsel review. The Other Sections Section I is one of four contiguous sections, each running beach to lagoon, together totalling 49,124.59 m² / 528,777 sq ft, roughly 4.91 hectares. The remaining three are available separately or alongside Section I, at the same USD $200 per square metre. Section I — this listing: 12,114.34 m² / 130,399 sq ft, USD $2,422,868 Section II: 12,343.54 m² / 132,866 sq ft, USD $2,468,708 Section III: 12,157.33 m² / 130,862 sq ft, USD $2,431,466 Section IV: 12,509.38 m² / 134,651 sq ft, USD $2,501,876 The complete holding of all four sections is USD $9,824,918. Sections are available individually or together. Ownership The property sits within the federal restricted coastal zone. Foreign buyers acquire through a fideicomiso (bank trust), the structure that conveys full rights of use, lease, improvement and sale. Our team coordinates the trust setup and the permit review alongside your counsel. 📍 Location: Coastal strip of the Sian Ka'an Biosphere Reserve, south of Tulum, Quintana Roo 🌴 Position: Section I, running full width from Caribbean beachfront to lagoon ⛲️ Features: Construction permits in place per the owner, with documentation available for review Owner support through the build and through further permitting Runs beach to lagoon across the full width of the peninsula Direct Caribbean beachfront with untouched white sand Lagoon frontage with existing timber dock Native palm forest and mature coastal vegetation Inside the Sian Ka'an Biosphere Reserve, a UNESCO World Heritage Site Coastal sand road access along the peninsula Surveyed and sectioned with full metes and bounds documentation Three further sections available separately or alongside 📏 Section I Lot Size sqm: 12,114.34 m² 📐 Section I Lot Size: 130,399 sq ft 💵 Price x m²: USD $200 💵 Section I Price: USD $2,422,868 💵 All four sections: 49,124.59 m² at USD $9,824,918
